Added

🔐 End-to-end encrypted chats. Direct messages and private group channels can now hold a temporary end-to-end encrypted chat: a member picks Encrypted Chat in the channel menu, the other members see "Encrypted chat in progress" with a Join link, messages of up to 16 KiB are encrypted in the browser with MLS and only passed through the server without being saved, participants can verify each other by comparing codes and see when others are typing, and the chat is cleared when you leave or reload and ends when channel membership or access changes. Administrators turn it on under Admin Settings > General > Encrypted channels or with "ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_CHANNELS" and grant it with the new Encrypted Channels permission, off by default or set with "USER_PERMISSIONS_FEATURES_ENCRYPTED_CHANNELS", and it needs websocket connections with websocket server logging off and HTTPS in production. Commit, Commit, Commit, Commit
📡 Much lighter streaming with Redis. With Redis, a streaming reply is now stored under its own key and new text is appended to it instead of rewriting the whole reply into a shared hash on every update, and replies started on older instances are still read during an upgrade; with room channels on, each instance now only subscribes to the rooms of people connected to it, so Redis no longer sends it live updates for chats it does not serve. Commit Commit #32478
🔍 Compare view options and undo. The Compare revision view has a Comparison options menu to ignore whitespace, ignore emphasis markers or only show changes with the unchanged lines folded away, an Undo button that steps back through your edits in both panes in order, and changed lines that are now lined up by their matching text. Commit, Commit, Commit, Commit
📝 Richer Markdown file previews. Markdown files opened in the terminal file browser now render with the same renderer as chat replies, including math, footnotes, highlighted code blocks, alerts and Mermaid diagrams, as well as HTML blocks mixed with Markdown, laid out as a compact document, and task list checkboxes in an editable file can be ticked to save the change to the file. Commit Commit Commit #32514
👀 Live collaborators in shared chats. The top bar of a chat now shows the pictures of the other people who have the same chat open at that moment, up to three and a count for the rest, with a Collaborators list that opens their profile cards. Commit, Commit, Commit
✏️ Edit and regenerate in shared chats with replies. In a chat from a shared folder that allows replies, people who may edit messages can now edit a prompt to start a new branch and regenerate any reply, not only replies to their own messages, and others viewing the chat stay on the branch they had selected. Commit, Commit
🗄️ Folder access in the folder editor. Sharing a folder now happens through an Access button in the Edit Folder dialog instead of a Share item in the folder menu, the sharing mode can be set before anyone is added, and subfolders note that access granted to parent folders also applies to them. Commit, Commit
🔎 Workspace search. The search window now searches your chats, chats in folders shared with you, chats shared with you, channel and direct messages and notes in one place, with filters for content type, a folder or channel, and whether something was created by you or shared with you, highlighted matches, a preview of each result with Ctrl/Cmd + Enter, Copy link, and channel results that open the thread scrolled to the matching message. Commit, Commit, Commit
💭 Comments in document previews. Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files opened in the terminal file browser now show their comments and replies, marked where they belong in the document and opened by hovering or tapping a marker, and older .xls spreadsheets can now be previewed too. Commit
🧹 Clear Input Selections shortcut. Clearing the model override, selected tools and filters and the web search, image generation and code interpreter toggles from the chat input is now a shortcut you can change in Settings > Shortcuts, still Escape by default. Commit
🙋 Ask about a file from the file browser. Selecting text in a file open in the terminal file browser now shows an "Ask or edit…" box that sends your request to the model with the file attached and the selection quoted, so it can answer or edit that file in the same terminal; unsaved edits can be saved before sending, and requests sent while a reply is running wait in the queue. Commit
☁️ Google Drive access limited to picked files. The Google Drive picker now asks only for access to the files a user picks instead of read access to their whole Drive, so self-hosted installs no longer need Google's restricted-scope verification and users no longer see the "Google hasn't verified this app" warning. #32531 Commit #29537
📜 Full text of long status lines. Status lines above a reply, such as a token usage summary sent by a function, can now be clicked to show their full text, and with several status lines the history shows every entry in full. #32532 Commit #30056
📏 Skill read limits. Administrators can set how many characters of a skill the model reads at once and how long the preview of longer instructions is, under Admin Settings > General with "Skill Read Limit" and "Skill Preview Length" or the "SKILL_CONTENT_MAX_CHARS" and "SKILL_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS" environment variables, which default to 20000 and 5000. Commit
🔄 General improvements. Various improvements were implemented across the application to enhance performance, stability, and security.
🌐 Translation updates. Translations for Portuguese (Brazil), Chinese (Traditional), Arabic, Bengali, Hebrew, Georgian, Punjabi, Slovak, Serbian, Urdu, Uzbek and Vietnamese were enhanced and expanded. #32440, #32482, #32501

Added

🤝 Keep both changes when comparing. The Compare revision view now has a Keep both button that puts the original and the proposed text of the selected change into the proposed revision, original first, so you no longer have to pick one side. Commit
📚 Open attached knowledge from its preview. Clicking the name in the preview of an attached knowledge collection now opens that collection in the workspace, and file and link names are real links that open in a new tab. Commit
🏷️ Model ID in custom headers. Custom headers on connections and tool servers can now use {{MODEL_ID}}, which holds the ID of the model handling the chat request, the workspace model's own ID for a workspace model and each model's own ID in a multi-model chat, so downstream services can route or log usage per model. #32426, Commit, #30006
🧾 Requested model in the audit log. Audit log entries for chat and completion requests, including the OpenAI, Ollama and Anthropic compatible endpoints, now carry a model_id field with the model the client asked for at every AUDIT_LOG_LEVEL, where the model only appeared in the request body and went missing when MAX_BODY_LOG_SIZE cut a long prompt; other requests log it as null. #32429, Commit, #30097
🔐 Custom TLS certificate for Milvus. Open WebUI can now connect to a Milvus server with a self-signed or company-issued TLS certificate by pointing the new "MILVUS_SERVER_PEM_PATH" environment variable at the certificate file, in normal and multi-tenancy mode. #32427, Commit, #31632
🧭 call_tool for Tool Search. With Tool Search on, the model now gets a new call_tool tool and runs a tool it found with search_tools through it, passing the tool's name and its arguments, instead of calling the deferred tool directly by a name that is not in the request's tool list, which strict providers rejected; approvals and other tool behavior stay the same. Commit, #32243
🔄 General improvements. Various improvements were implemented across the application to enhance performance, stability, and security.

Fixed

🔏 Channel message metadata kept server side. Channel messages posted or edited through the API no longer take their metadata from the request, so a user can no longer make a message appear to come from a channel webhook or a model. #32421, Commit
👮 SCIM cannot delete admins. An identity provider can no longer delete administrator accounts, including the first admin, through a SCIM delete request, which now answers with 403 and leaves the account in place, so a sync that prunes unassigned users can no longer leave the instance without an administrator; admins are removed in the admin panel. #32415, Commit, #27662
🗝️ Collection names checked as stored. Retrieval access checks now compare collection names the way vector stores resolve them, ignoring letter case and treating hyphens and underscores alike, so a name written differently can no longer pass the check as something other than the collection that is then read. #32435, Commit
📱 Voice on Android Chrome. Voice calls and dictation on Android Chrome no longer go silent or hang on Listening after about ten uses until the page is reloaded, since the microphone level display now releases its audio output after each turn. #32417, Commit, #29969
🖥️ Per chat terminal file actions. With the Open Terminal chat context set to Per chat, opening HTML files, running notebooks, saving edited files, creating new files, deleting several selected files and downloading a folder or selection as a zip now use the chat's own workspace, where HTML files showed "File not found" and saved files never appeared in the chat. #32418, Commit, #29965
🧮 Memory reindex rate limits. Reindexing memories, from the admin Reindex Knowledge and Memory Vectors button, a user resetting their memory vectors or the automatic reindex after an embedding model change, now follows the Embedding Concurrent Requests limit and batch size, where it sent one request per memory at once and rate-limited providers failed most of them with 429 errors. #32420, Commit, #32212
⏰ Automation run results. An automation run is now recorded as successful only after its reply finishes, and a reply that fails or is cancelled is recorded as an error that links to the chat, where runs counted as successful as soon as the reply started. Commit
📜 Long polling kept out of the audit log. With websocket support turned off, every socket.io long polling request is no longer written to the audit log as its own entry, which flooded it and could not be filtered with AUDIT_EXCLUDED_PATHS, so the audit log looks the same with either transport. #32425, Commit, #31871
📎 Sources of approved tools. With tool approval set to ask, a knowledge or file tool the user approved now saves and shows its sources below the reply, where they were lost after approval. #32439, Commit, #32436
🗂️ Sidebar hover previews. Moving the pointer from one sidebar folder to the next no longer leaves the first folder's preview open or keeps the next one from opening, and folder and chat previews now also open when the pointer rests on the padding around a name. #32438, Commit, #32437

Sign In  All articles October 10, 2026 / 22 MINUTES READ Open WebUI v0.12.0: A Voice That Talks Back, and a Face to Go With It   SUMMARY v0.12.0 puts a realtime voice on the line that answers as quickly as a person and hands every real question to the model you already chose, with its history and tools. The voice can wear an animated 3D avatar, and administrators get multi-factor sign-in, groups inside groups, and a knob for how hard a model thinks. Shared chats can take replies from everyone they're shared with, and every saved model, tool, and skill keeps its earlier versions.  If you've used Voice mode, you know its rhythm. You speak and the transcript goes to your model. The whole reply gets written, and only then does text-to-speech read it back. The loop works, though a conversation through it never quite feels like talking to someone.Open WebUI v0.12.0 changes who picks up the call. A realtime voice model now holds the conversation, and every question that needs real work goes to the model you already chose, tools and all. The voice can also wear a face. By the end, you'll know which switches turn all of this on and where each one lives. If you run Milvus, or several instances that share websocket traffic through Redis, read the Before you upgrade section first. There's plenty more in the changelog, which runs to more than forty additions and over two hundred seventy fixes.A voice that talks back #Voice calls get a second mode. Under Admin Settings, the Audio page now opens on a Voice calls section, where Call mode switches from Standard to Realtime. In Realtime mode, Voice mode talks through an OpenAI Realtime voice model, gpt-realtime-2.1-mini with the marin voice unless you pick another. Setting Call mode to Realtime reveals the connection, voice, and prompt fields for the voice modelYour own model stays in the loop. The voice model keeps small talk to itself and passes anything that needs real work to the model picked for the chat. Small talk stays with the voice model, while a real question makes the orange round trip through your own modelThe conversation moves at the pace of a phone call, while the knowledge base, web search, or terminal you've set up still does the work behind it. When a tool needs approval or the model asks you something, the voice points you to the chat, because a spoken yes doesn't approve a tool. The base URL is yours to set, for any endpoint that speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol, and calls need the Allow Call permission.A face to go with it #A voice call doesn't have to show an orb. With Realtime mode on, the model editor's Voice section gains two rows. Realtime Voice lets a model speak in its own voice, while the voice model itself stays the administrator's choice. Voice avatar gives the model a 3D character for its calls. The new Skills switch under Builtin Tools, and the Realtime Voice and Voice avatar rows in the Voice sectionThe Configure button on the Voice avatar row opens Avatar setup, where you can upload a VRM file of up to 25 MiB. VRM is the open format VTubers and social VR apps use for 3D characters, and the editor accepts both its 0.x and 1.0 versions. The preview cycles through Idle, Listening, and Speaking, the three states a call moves between. Built-in motion keeps an avatar with no animations of its own breathing, swaying, and blinking.


A VRM 1.0 avatar loads in Avatar setup and moves through its Idle, Listening, and Speaking poses on built-in motionYou can replace each state's movement with a VRMA clip of up to 10 MiB. You can also add up to 16 named gestures, each with a short clip and a description of when it fits. The voice model reads those names and descriptions and plays a wave or a clap on its own when the moment calls for one. A wave gesture, described so the voice model knows when to use itDuring a call, the mouth moves with the loudness of the spoken answer. The avatar appears only in Realtime calls, and a model without one keeps the orb.A second step at sign-in #An instance that's reachable from the internet can now ask for more than a password. Turn on Require an authenticator for all users under Admin Settings > Authentication, and every account sets up an authenticator app on its next sign-in. The interface calls this multi-factor authentication. Turning the switch on signs every device out, your own included. The new Multi-factor authentication section, with the main switch on and both bypass switches offThe next sign-in starts with a QR code. Scan it with any authenticator app, enter the six-digit code it shows, and Open WebUI hands back ten single-use recovery codes to download and keep somewhere safe.


A user signs in with a password, scans the QR code, enters the code from the authenticator app, saves the recovery codes, and lands in a chat The setup screen (left) and the recovery codes (right), each shown onceFrom then on, every sign-in asks for a code after the password. Use a recovery code takes one of the saved codes instead, and each code works once. Each person manages their own authenticator and recovery codes from Account settingsTwo more switches can let OAuth and trusted-header sign-ins through without the extra step, for an identity provider that already enforces its own. If you're closing off an account you suspect has leaked, remove its API keys too.Reply in a shared chat #People you share a chat with can now write in it, rather than reading a frozen copy or cloning it into chats of their own. Once a chat is shared with someone, the Share Chat dialog shows a Sharing mode setting. Switching the setting from Clone only to Allow replies lets everyone the chat is shared with keep the same conversation going. Folders shared with people or groups get the same setting, which only the owner or an administrator can change. A chat shared with the Engineering group, with Sharing mode set to Allow repliesMessages from other people show the sender's name and profile picture. Answers stream to everyone who has the chat open, and a line above the message box shows who's typing. The owner's view, with Sam's question on the left under Sam's name and Sam typing the next oneEach message is answered under the account of the person who sent it, with the models and permissions that person already has. Next to SKILL.md, a skill can carry scripts, references, and templates in a file tree inside the skill editor, and whole skills import from and export to ZIP or JSON. With Community Sharing on in Admin Settings > General, people allowed to export skills can send one to openwebui.com, files and all, from Share in its menu. A skill opened from openwebui.com loads straight into the skill editor for anyone allowed to import skills. Share opens the Create post page on openwebui.com with the skill and its files already filled in, ready to postModels can read a skill's files and edit any skill the person chatting is allowed to change. Anyone allowed to create workspace skills can also turn a chat into a new skill with /skills:create, which no longer needs a terminal.The Skills switch under a model's Builtin Tools is on by default. Turning it off stops that model from looking up, reading, editing, or creating skills, while skills someone picks for a chat still apply.Control how hard a model thinks #Reasoning models let you trade speed for depth, and until now making that trade meant a trip into advanced parameters. Anyone who can edit a model can now attach Model controls to it, from the row just below Advanced Params in the model editor. A control has a name and a set of options, and each option carries its own parameters. One option can be the default, and the control shows as a menu or as a slider. A Thinking control with three options, each setting Ollama's think level, shown as a slider with Medium as the defaultPeople then pick an option from a new Model controls button beside the model selector in the chat input. The choice is saved to their account, so it follows them to other devices. The menu in chat shows only the labels, while the parameter values behind them stay in the model editor. The model selector in v0.11.4 (left) and v0.12.0 (right), with the new Model controls button beside the model nameWe set up a Thinking control on gpt-oss:20b through Ollama and asked the same arithmetic puzzle at each end of the slider:ThinkingTokens writtenReasoningAnswerLow2530 charactersRightHigh209624 charactersRight  That's one question and one run at each setting, so read it as a demonstration rather than a benchmark.

Automations run with each control's default option rather than anyone's personal pick.Groups inside groups #A group can now have a parent. Members of the inner group get everything shared with the groups above it, along with those groups' permissions. A company can share a model with everyone once and still give each team its own settings. The groups list in v0.11.4 (left) and v0.12.0 (right), where the same three groups now form a treeThe group editor marks inherited permissions, and switching off a permission locally doesn't take away one that comes from a parent. Open browsers pick up changed access right away, without a reload.Groups can also set Default models for new chats, which their members get instead of the instance-wide default. When several groups apply, the most deeply nested one wins, and a model someone picked as their own default still comes first. Platform's settings, with Engineering as its parent and the default model it inherits from EngineeringOn our test instance, we shared three models with Acme only and put Sam in Platform, two levels down. Sam saw all three models, and a new chat opened on the model Engineering set as its default.Smaller prompts with many tools #Every tool a model can call, built-in tools included, sends its full definition with each request. Those definitions can outweigh the conversation itself. Tool Search, marked experimental in Admin Settings > Interface, keeps any definition longer than the Deferral Threshold out of the request, and the threshold starts at 400 characters. The model gets those tools as a list of names with short descriptions, plus a search_tools tool that fetches a full definition when the model needs one. A knowledge base now opens as a file browser, with its folders and files on the left and the selected file beside them. Switching between Preview and Indexed text shows the original document or the text the model searches, and anyone with write access can edit that text in place. On its first start, Open WebUI copies every existing Milvus collection into a new one that holds the vectors, the text, and the keyword index together.
